sources.title: DreamWAM: Beyond RGB Future Prediction for World Action Models

sectionsRead: Appendix A.1–A.2: target construction and inference (p. 10)
Appendix B.1–B.4: real-world data, tasks, perturbations and success (pp. 10–11)
omissions: Verified edition: arXiv:2608.04996v1, 5 August 2026. Title and all nine authors agree with the catalog. No alternative revision was supplied or compared.
Text extraction does not reconstruct figure images; inspect the retained PDF for figures and equation/table layout.
The extraction limitation was addressed by visually inspecting Figures 1–3, Tables 1–3, and all pages supporting retained scientific claims. Reference pages 8–9 were read as text only.
Separate supplemental material availability has not been fully verified.
Code, linked project resources and models were not inspected; no experiments were reproduced.

synopsis: DreamWAM trains coupled video and action experts to anticipate appearance, motion, geometry and semantics, while retaining RGB-only deployment. Its strongest evidence is improved executed-task success under unseen perturbations, including when future video rollout is disabled. Routing heterogeneous targets matters as much as adding them.

problem.text: RGB prediction can entangle task-relevant changes with texture, illumination and background. The authors propose richer future targets to preserve movement, spatial relationships and object identity under shifts that leave the required manipulation unchanged.

contributions.text: Combine RGB–motion latent denoising with gated residual prediction of geometry and semantics in a coupled VideoDiT–ActionDiT policy.
Matched no-rollout and joint evaluations separate benefits learned during training from benefits of online RGB imagination; routing controls test whether extra supervision alone suffices.

inputs: Language instruction and current RGB observation at deployment
Training demonstrations with future RGB clips and action chunks; offline teacher-derived future targets
outputs: Future RGB latents in joint inference; motion and feature predictions only during training

steps.name: Construct aligned future targets
steps.detail: Frozen RAFT estimates eight adjacent flows from nine frames. Colorized flow duplicates its first transition to form nine frames; the frozen Wan2.2 VAE encodes it as 48×3×14×28. These are image-space motion features, not raw metric vectors.

steps.name: Compress geometry and semantics
steps.detail: DA3-Base processes individual camera views before depth maps are reassembled, log-transformed and reduced by rank-8 PCA. Frozen DINOv2 ViT-B/14 with registers supplies normalized 768-dimensional patch features, also reduced to eight dimensions. Both use training-only PCA, a 14×28 grid and temporal groups: frame 1, mean of 2–5, mean of 6–9. DINO features receive channel normalization.

steps.name: Route according to representation
steps.detail: RGB and VAE-encoded flow enter channel-concatenated denoising. Geometry and semantics instead produce gated additive corrections at selected video layers, preserving the original block output. Their teachers supply targets rather than policy observations.

steps.name: Transfer future structure into actions
steps.detail: Separate video and action experts contribute tokens to shared attention, then apply their own projections and feed-forward transformations. ActionDiT denoises actions using this shared representation without directly consuming teacher features.

training.text: The loss combines RGB/motion/action flow matching, geometry/semantic prediction and L1 gate regularization. Auxiliary objectives update the shared video backbone; teacher encoders and the target VAE are frozen.

Matched simulation variants use Wan2.2-5B, eight NVIDIA H20 GPUs, bfloat16, learning rate 1×10⁻⁵ and batch size 16. Only original LIBERO demonstrations are used. Real-world models share 1,600 pooled demonstrations in LeRobot v2.1 format and train for five epochs.

inference.text: DreamWAM jointly denoises future RGB and actions; DreamWAM-uncond keeps only the first-frame video input and denoises actions without video rollout. The 32-step action policy executes ten steps before replanning, using ten denoising steps.

Flow input channels are zero-filled; RAFT, DA3, DINOv2, residual branches and prediction heads are not executed. Training also zeros conditioning-frame flow, but applies flow loss to future steps. The control output remains the action chunk.

equations.explanation: Eq. (2): z is the target latent, x its perturbed version, t the shared flow-matching timestep, and epsilon the perturbation term. Concat_C joins channels. The source does not specify the perturbation distribution here.

equations.expression: \bar h_\ell=B_\ell(h_{\ell-1}),\qquad h_\ell=\bar h_\ell+\sum_{j\in\{\mathrm{geo},\mathrm{sem}\}}g_\ell^j(\bar h_\ell,c)\odot R_\ell^j(\bar h_\ell),\qquad \hat f^j=P_j(h_L)
equations.explanation: Eq. (3): B is the original block; bar h its output; R a view-specific residual; g its gate conditioned on the state and instruction c. Elementwise gated corrections produce h. P predicts aligned features from final state h_L.

Eq. (4): lambda terms weight flow-matching, feature-prediction and gate losses; the gate term penalizes gate activations with an L1 norm. Numerical weights and exact feature-loss formulas are unspecified.

Appendix Eqs. (8)–(10): the input projection W partitions into RGB and flow groups; b is its bias and z_RGB^0 encodes the current observation. Zero flow contributes no input signal, although learned shared parameters retain training effects.

results.setting: Four ten-task suites; 50 rollouts/task, 2,000/seed; two seeds; original demonstrations only.
results.interpretation: Small mean gains near ceiling; joint Goal falls from 98.80 to 98.60, so improvement is not universal across suites.

results.setting: Seven unseen perturbation dimensions; 10,030 episodes/seed, two seeds; no perturbation training data.
results.metric: Unweighted mean of seven dimension success rates (%)
results.interpretation: All seven columns improve in each pair. From printed averages, gains are 12.08 and 6.31 percentage points. Prose gives 12.09 for no-rollout; underlying rounding is unresolved.

results.setting: AgileX PiPER; four tasks, 30 trials each; matched joint models trained on the same demonstrations.
results.interpretation: All four plotted task scores improve; success requires the complete sequence and stable final placements.

results.setting: Lighting, background and distractor/layout changes separately; 30 trials each; no adaptation or perturbed demonstrations.
results.interpretation: Evidence concerns three visual shifts on one trained task, not new skills or combined perturbations.

results.setting: Matched joint training; all variants retain RGB; two seeds under the standard simulation protocol.
results.comparison: RGB only 98.00; all-denoise D/D/D 97.85; without motion 97.50, geometry 98.25, semantics 98.60.
results.interpretation: Compatible routing matters; adding all targets through denoising underperforms RGB only. Motion removal hurts most, but these near-ceiling results do not establish perturbation-specific causal mechanisms.

limitations.text: These targets are correlated projections, not complete physical state: motion is colorized 2D flow; depth is compressed; semantics are features, not labels. Metric 3D and contact-aware targets remain future work.

Simulation tables give two-seed means without dispersion; real settings have 30 trials and no confidence intervals. Heterogeneous external baselines are contextual, while matched Fast-WAM comparisons provide stronger controls. The single pictured failure cannot isolate causation.

Figure 2 shows separate feature-output additions, whereas Eq. (3) writes both predictors from h_L; exact head wiring remains unclear. Its five-loss summary also omits the gate penalty explicitly included in Eq. (4).

reproduction.text: Recover loss weights, feature-loss definitions, selected residual layers, gate initialization and simulation training duration before claiming a faithful reproduction. The source also lacks a complete optimizer/scheduler specification and measured deployment latency.

Proposed checks: repeat D/R/R versus D/D/D with identical targets and seeds under LIBERO-Plus; separately compare both inference modes with auxiliary computation disabled. Report task-level outcomes and uncertainty, not only averages.

reasoning.text: Separate VideoDiT and ActionDiT parameters support Dual-system; shared attention and concurrent video/action denoising support Joint prediction and Q3, rather than inverse-dynamics action extraction. Geometry and multiview preprocessing justify a qualified spatial tag, not a claim of metric 3D world reconstruction. No-rollout deployment does not erase joint predictive training.

discussionQuestions: Does the routing advantage persist under unseen perturbations with more seeds?
How much robustness survives temporal misalignment of motion targets?

evidence.location: PDF p. 1, title block and arXiv margin stamp
evidence.detail: The title and all nine authors match the catalog; the supplied edition is arXiv:2608.04996v1, 5 August 2026. Four institutions are credited.
The authors motivate appearance, motion, geometry and semantics using manipulation under visual shifts; the pictured rollouts are qualitative examples.

evidence.location: PDF p. 3, Method: Preliminaries, Structured Future Views, Eqs. (1)–(2)
evidence.detail: Language and observations condition coupled video/action learning. RGB and motion latents share a denoising timestep and are concatenated by channel; geometry and semantics are training targets.

evidence.location: PDF p. 4, Figure 2/caption and Gated residual modeling, Eq. (3)
evidence.detail: Gated view-specific residuals add to the original block output; the equation predicts both feature views from the final shared state. The schematic draws separate feature-output addition nodes.
VideoDiT and ActionDiT retain separate parameters, sharing attention context at paired layers before separate projections and feed-forward transformations.

evidence.location: PDF p. 5, Training Objective and Inference, Eq. (4)
evidence.detail: The objective weights RGB, motion, geometry, semantics, action and an L1 gate-activation penalty. Non-RGB branches and teachers are inactive at deployment.

Original LIBERO training only; four ten-task suites, 500 demonstrations per suite, two seeds, 2,000 standard and 10,030 perturbed episodes per seed. Matched models use Wan2.2-5B and the same action policy and training setup.

evidence.location: PDF p. 5, Table 1, matched four rows, suite and Avg. columns
evidence.detail: No-rollout averages are 97.30/98.40 and joint averages 98.00/98.90 for Fast-WAM/DreamWAM; some individual suites do not improve.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Table 2, matched WAM rows, seven perturbation columns and Avg.; LIBERO-Plus discussion
evidence.detail: Matched no-rollout averages are 51.36/63.44 and joint averages 69.16/75.47. Both pairs improve in all seven columns; prose reports a 12.09-point no-rollout gain.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Table 3, all rows; p. 7, Ablation Study continuation
evidence.detail: D denotes full denoising and R gated residual injection. RGB only scores 98.00, D/D/D 97.85 and D/R/R 98.90; paired single-view and omission controls test routing and complementarity.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Figure 3/caption; p. 6, Real-World Robot results
evidence.detail: Four standard-task bars and three perturbation bars compare the two joint models. Reported means are 90.8/96.7 and 55.6/74.4; a qualitative failure concerns gripper-to-plate alignment.
Frozen RAFT and Wan VAE encode colorized flow as 48×3×14×28. DA3-Base depth and DINOv2 ViT-B/14 with registers are reduced with training-only PCA and aligned as 8×3×14×28.

Zero flow channels contribute nothing through the input projection. Conditioning-frame flow is also zero during training; future latent steps receive the flow objective. Teachers, residual branches and heads are not executed at deployment.

evidence.location: PDF p. 10, Appendix B.1, Eq. (11); p. 5, Experimental Setup: Real robot
evidence.detail: AgileX PiPER dual-arm evaluation uses 400 demonstrations per task, 1,600 total, LeRobot v2.1 and five epochs. Each model receives 30 trials per setting, 210 overall; standard and perturbation means are separate.

Four tasks specify ordered placement/stacking. Strawberry perturbations separately change colored background patches, fill lighting and irrelevant distractor objects. Complete sequences and stable final placements are required; there is no partial credit.

evidence.location: PDF p. 3, Structured Future Views; p. 7, Conclusion
evidence.detail: Future views are neither a disentangled nor complete physical state. Metric 3D and contact-aware targets are proposed future work.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 4–5, Method and Experimental Setup; p. 10, Appendix A
evidence.detail: The supplied implementation description gives losses, target construction and basic training settings but does not specify loss weights, exact residual-layer placement, gate initialization, feature-loss formulas or simulation training duration.
